item.title: EP07: Information Entropy and All-Interval Rows
item.description: Overview A listener hears two melodies and judges the second as “more chaotic.” But when you measure the distribution of adjacent intervals, the second melody is mathematically more uniform — its Shannon entropy is higher, not lower. The discomfort comes not from disorder but from the absence of the familiar concentrated pattern that tonal music trains the brain to expect. This episode builds Shannon’s entropy from first principles and applies it to music.
